macro_events: OIL EASES ON DIPLOMACY HOPES: Brent fell ~3.9% to $96.72 on 24-Jul (intraday ~$95), off the $100+ spike, after reports that Pakistan - with Chinese support - is seeking to revive US-Iran negotiations; Chinese officials are said to be increasingly concerned that Gulf disruptions are hurting their economy. Crude still ended the week up ~8%. A fading oil spike is a modest smelter-cost relief. (Trading Economics; Reuters)

STRIKES CONTINUE, RHETORIC HOT: US Central Command carried out a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, targeting military and maritime infrastructure; the US says Hormuz 'remains open with American support'. President Trump warned he was weighing an 'unprecedented' / 'massive' military response and severe retaliation for any further Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping. Escalation and de-escalation tracks now run in parallel. (CNBC; Reuters)

RED SEA & KAZAKH OIL: Houthi attacks on two Saudi tankers have pushed Asian buyers to reroute Saudi crude via Suez and around Africa, and the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended Black Sea loadings after tanker attacks, disrupting ~80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports - alternative routes are themselves under stress. (Trading Economics; Reuters)

INVENTORY FLOOR HOLDS: LME aluminium stock drew to 275,175 t on the 23-Jul official (~-46% YTD), a fresh low since 2022, with SHFE also drawing; Macquarie flags a ~930 kt 2026 deficit. The physical-tightness case is intact beneath the softer flat price. (Westmetall; alcircle)

ALUMINA RELIEF RAMPING: EGA's Al Taweelah refinery has been at full alumina output since 10-Jul, targeting 50% of capacity within days and full capability by end-2026; ex-China alumina eased to ~$322/t FOB Australia as the surplus deepens - the principal supply-side counterweight. (EGA; SMM)

US TRADE POLICY: Section 232 stays at 50% on covered aluminium (eff. 08-Jun through 31-Dec-2027); a new 20-Jul incentive program grants approved US-investing producers a half-rate on tied primary imports. At the 23-Jul cash of $3,194 the tariff leg is ~$1,597/t - the largest administered component of the US duty-paid premium. (White House; CBP)
lme_commentary: At this Saturday 25-Jul refresh the latest PUBLISHED LME official is the 23-Jul settlement (cash $3,194.00 / 3M $3,182.00 / stock 275,175 t); the LME is closed for the weekend and Monday 27-Jul is the next session. The 23-Jul official eased after two firm sessions - cash -$11.00 (-0.34%) and 3M -$3.00 (-0.09%) - narrowing the cash-3M backwardation to +$12.00 from +$20.00, and the traded 3M slipped further to ~$3,165 on 24-Jul (Trading Economics). The driver was a narrowing war-risk premium: Brent fell ~4% toward $96 after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran talks, even as US Central Command ran a 13th straight night of strikes and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'. Structurally the market stays tight - LME stock at 275,175 t is the lowest since 2022 and ~46% below the start of the year, SHFE stocks are drawing, and the curve is still backwardated (+$12) - so the pullback reads as a pause, not a reversal, holding the rebound off the early-July $3,085 four-month low. Copper eased to a $13,741/t 3M official (23-Jul) from ~$13,876. Norsk Hydro's Q2 beat (22-Jul, adjusted EBITDA NOK 8.9bn) confirms producers are capturing the higher price and premiums. The supply counterweights are building - EGA's Al Taweelah alumina refinery at full output since 10-Jul and a China export arb that has narrowed - so the near-term skew has swung from one-way escalation back to two-sided. Monday's official is the next read on whether the front re-steepens or the premium keeps unwinding.

alumina_notes: The alumina market remains the mirror image of metal: globally LOOSENING (EGA's 2.4 Mtpa restart at full output since 10-Jul, Guinea bauxite oversupply, Chinese port stocks building; SMM Alumina Index easing toward ~Y2,700/t) - ex-China consolidation has slipped to ~$300-322 (FOB Australia ~$322, from ~$328).

The regional wrinkle persists but is easing: the shipping disruption still spans two waterways (a strained Hormuz plus Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea), yet the war-risk cover embedded in the ~60% of Gulf alumina imports that transit Hormuz is re-pricing lower at the margin as Brent comes off $100 and US-Iran talks are floated. SMM separately flags ex-China metallurgical-grade output down ~6% y/y in June.

Guinea's pending export-quota policy (a considered cap near 150 Mt for 2026, vs 178 Mt shipped in 2025, targeting >$100/dmt bauxite) remains undecreed and is the one clear bullish catalyst on the commodity leg; record Australian and Metro Mining shipments underline how long the seaborne bauxite market currently is.
net_read: TIGHT MARKET, WAR PREMIUM NARROWING, SKEW BACK TO TWO-SIDED. The flat price paused its rebound: the latest published 23-Jul official is cash $3,194.00 / 3M $3,182.00 with the cash-3M backwardation NARROWED to +$12.00 (from +$20.00) and stock at a fresh 2022 low of 275,175 t (~-46% YTD). The curve is still backwardated - physical tightness is intact - but the war-risk premium began to unwind: Brent fell ~4% toward $96 on 24-Jul after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is trying to revive US-Iran talks, even as US strikes ran a 13th straight night and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'. Roughly 9% of global primary supply still sits behind Hormuz and the Red Sea, so the floor is real; the offsets are also building - EGA's Al Taweelah alumina ramp (full output since 10-Jul), a deepening ex-China alumina surplus (~$322 FOB Australia), and a SHFE/LME arb that has narrowed enough to threaten the record China export flow. Norsk Hydro's Q2 beat (22-Jul, adjusted EBITDA NOK 8.9bn) shows the price/premium capture reaching producer margins. Net: a genuinely tight market whose near-term skew has swung from one-way escalation back to two-sided, with the diplomacy track (Pakistan/China) now the key downside trigger and the 2022-low inventory the floor.

US POLICY TWEAK: A new Section-232 incentive program lets approved companies investing in US primary-aluminium capacity import metal tied to expected output at half the 50% rate - a first, targeted crack in the administered US tariff wall (White House; CBP).

news.headline: Brent fell ~3.9% to $96.72 on 24-Jul (intraday ~$95) after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran negotiations - raising hopes of a diplomatic off-ramp and trimming the war-risk premium across metals, even as US Central Command ran a 13th straight night of strikes and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'. Two-sided again, not one-way.

LME aluminium stock drew another 1,600 t to 275,175 t on the 23-Jul official, a fresh low since 2022 (~-46% YTD), with SHFE stocks also falling. Macquarie flags a ~930 kt 2026 deficit. Inventories kept drawing even as the flat price eased - no buffer against a fresh interruption.

The SHFE/LME price ratio recovered last week, sharply narrowing the export margins that drove record H1 semis exports (June 711 kt; H1 +16.3% y/y). New orders are softening and semis-export flow faces reduction risk if margins stay compressed - a potential loosening of the export valve. Q2 GDP grew 4.3%.

EGA's Al Taweelah refinery has been at full alumina output since 10-Jul, ramping toward 50% of capacity and full capability by end-2026; ex-China alumina eased to ~$322/t FOB Australia as the surplus deepens. The principal supply-side offset to the geopolitical risk keeps building.

US Section 232 stays at 50% on covered aluminium (eff. 08-Jun through 31-Dec-2027); from 20-Jul a new incentive program lets approved US-investing producers import primary at half-rate. The US duty-paid premium stays policy-dominated (~$1,597/t tariff at the 23-Jul $3,194 LME cash).

earnings.headline: Revenue $3.97bn (+24% q/q, highest in nearly a decade); adj. EPS $2.12 (MISS vs ~$2.31 consensus); adj. net income $562m; adj. EBITDA $901m (from $595m in Q1); Aluminum segment RECORD EBITDA $1.073bn at 32.3% margin.
earnings.readthrough: First producer P&L under the Hormuz-disruption regime: record aluminium margins and near-decade-high revenue on higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums, but adj. EPS missed on higher costs — notably ~$35m more Section-232 tariff on Canadian metal into the US — and the shares fell. South32 upstream acquisition ($4.1bn upfront, up to $5.6bn contingent to 2030) progressing, close expected H1-2027. The tariff is a double edge: it inflates US premia but taxes Alcoa's cross-border Canadian metal.

earnings.headline: Q2 2026 BEAT: adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y vs NOK 7,790m; above consensus); Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 6,421m; adjusted EPS NOK 2.2 (from NOK 1.7); free cash flow NOK 4bn; 12-month adjusted RoaCE 10.9%. Shares rose on the print.
earnings.readthrough: First European producer P&L of the Hormuz-disruption quarter. Higher aluminium prices and product premiums plus stronger recycling earnings drove the beat; a stronger NOK and lower hydro-power output were partial offsets. Confirms the disruption-quarter price/premium is translating into real producer margin - a positive read-across for the smelter complex.

earnings.headline: Adj. EPS $1.63 (beat $1.56); revenue $649m; net income $327m (incl. $288m Hawesville sale gain).

earnings.readthrough: LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.

earnings.readthrough: Kitimat, NZAS and AP60 continued their ramp-up while Arvida's final two potlines closed in June as planned, completing the transition to AP60. Steady low-carbon Canadian output into a tight, premium-rich market - constructive for realised margins even as the flat price eased.

earnings.readthrough: Resilient structural demand for Cu/Al cited; broadly constructive sector tone.

ai_analysis: The defining feature is a shift in the tape from one-way escalation to a two-sided setup: the 23-Jul official eased (cash $3,194.00 / 3M $3,182.00), narrowing the cash-3M backwardation to +$12.00, and on 24-Jul Brent fell ~4% toward $96 after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran talks. The war-risk premium that had been building began to unwind - even as US strikes ran a 13th straight night - so a market that was gapping higher is now consolidating.

The structural tightness is intact, not resolved: LME stock at 275,175 t is a fresh low since 2022 and roughly 46% below the start of the year, SHFE inventories are drawing, and the curve is still backwardated at +$12.00. Macquarie flags a ~930 kt 2026 deficit, wider than the Reuters poll's -365 kt. The offsets are building on the other side - EGA's Al Taweelah alumina at full output (10-Jul) with ex-China alumina easing to ~$322, and a SHFE/LME arb that has narrowed enough to threaten the record China export flow.

The corporate read still corroborates the price: Norsk Hydro's Q2 (22-Jul) beat with adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y) and the shares rose; Alcoa (16-Jul) posted record Aluminum-segment EBITDA but missed on EPS on Section-232 costs; South32 (20-Jul) beat FY26 production guidance; Rio Tinto (14-Jul) held aluminium at 841 kt with Arvida closed and AP60/Kitimat ramping. The disruption-quarter price and premiums are reaching real producer margin.

The swing variable has flipped: the de-escalation path (a durable ceasefire) is back on the table via the Pakistan/China track, which is now the prominent downside trigger, while the escalation path (continued strikes, Trump's 'massive attack' threat) remains live. Regionally the premium complex stays decoupled - Japan Q3 MJP $395/t (decade high), Rotterdam duty-unpaid ~$542.50/t with its war-risk leg easing, and the US duty-paid premium dominated by the 50% Section 232 rate (~$1,597/t at the 23-Jul cash), now with a new 20-Jul half-rate incentive for US-investing producers.

premium_explainer.desc: The physical-delivery adder over the LME price: regional logistics, duties/tariffs and local tightness — quoted $/t (or ¢/lb in the US) on top of LME cash. It is what converts an exchange price into a delivered price.

Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan (Platts, 06-Jul) - a decade high and the fourth straight rise ($86 -> $195 -> $351.5 -> $395). SMM flags spot tightness under the LME backwardation, though CIF spot eased to ~$365 with the narrowing risk premium. Q4 talks (~Sep) open against the decade-high anchor, but into a war premium that is fading rather than widening - a more two-sided Q4 than a week ago.

Platts duty-unpaid last publicly marked ~$525-560 (mid $542.50, 03-Jul). The 6% EU duty, CBAM and Mozal's care & maintenance keep the structural floor; the war-risk freight component is easing again as Brent comes off $100 and US-Iran talks are floated.

SMM's weekly DDP ~109.75 c/lb ~ $2,420/t (10-Jul); Platts MW Transaction ~108.7 c (03-Jul), Fastmarkets ~110-112 c (07-Jul). The 50% Section-232 tariff-$ leg (~$1,597 at the 23-Jul LME cash) dominates the all-in - US premia track Washington and the LME, not local tightness. A new 20-Jul incentive program grants approved US-investing producers a half-rate on tied primary imports.

The decomposition below separates the mechanical tariff leg (Section-232 rate x LME) from the residual market premium. Most of the US 'premium' is a policy transfer, not a scarcity signal - and the new half-rate incentive for US-investing producers (20-Jul) is the first targeted crack in that administered wall.

premium_outlook: Asian (MJP / CIF Japan): Q3 settled $395 (decade high, unchanged); CIF spot ~$365, eased as the risk premium narrowed. With US-Iran talks now floated, Q4 negotiations (~Sep) open against the $395 anchor into a more two-sided backdrop than a week ago - firm, but no longer one-way higher.

European (EDU): last public Platts mark ~$525-560 (mid $542.50, 03-Jul), unchanged. The 6% duty + CBAM floor plus Mozal's outage keep Europe structurally tighter than pre-war; the marginal driver - Gulf/Red Sea war-risk freight - is easing again as Brent comes off $100.

US Midwest: SMM DDP ~109.75 c/lb (10-Jul), unchanged. The tariff leg (50% x LME ~ $1,597 at the 23-Jul cash) is ~two-thirds of the all-in, so US premia track the LME and Washington more than Gulf events directly. A new 20-Jul incentive program grants approved US-investing producers a half-rate on tied primary imports - the first policy step that could compress the US premium. Watch the next weekly print.

long_term.label: Long-term — weekly (position degree)
long_term.writeup: LONG TERM (weekly / position). Count unchanged at the 25-Jul refresh - no invalidation break. It remains a completed five-wave impulse from the 2,300 base into the 3,855 high of 02-Jun-2026 (wave 5 extended, as commodities typically do), followed by a corrective A-B-C: A to 3,359, B to 3,406, C bottoming at 3,061.50 on 02-Jul, holding the .50 retracement at 3,077 within the 2,950-3,110 target zone. All three cardinal rules hold (wave 2 < 100% of wave 1; wave 3 not shortest; wave 4 no overlap with wave 1). BASE CASE still leans BULL (52%): a new impulse is building off 3,061.50, but the 23-Jul pullback (cash $3,194, 3M $3,182, backwardation narrowing to +$12) and the fading war premium temper conviction versus a week ago - a wave (i)/(ii) sequence rather than a clean breakout. A sustained weekly close above 3,260 opens 3,450 then the 3,620-3,780 zone. RANGE ALTERNATE (35%): the recovery holds between the 3,085 low and the 3,230-3,260 resistance stack as the war premium unwinds. BEAR ALTERNATE (13%): a durable Pakistan/China-brokered ceasefire releases the war premium and extends the correction toward the .618 at 2,894. INVALIDATION: a weekly close below 3,061.50 negates the completed-C reading; a decisive weekly close above 3,260 confirms the new impulse. CONFIDENCE: moderate - the .50 hold and 2022-low inventory support the bull lean, but the narrowing premium and the revived diplomacy track are the tail risk to watch. Technical context only, not advice.

short_term.label: Short-term — daily (swing degree)
short_term.writeup: SHORT TERM (daily / swing). Count unchanged at the 25-Jul refresh. The corrective sequence off the 3,855 high of 02-Jun counts as A to 3,359, B to 3,607 (the spike that was sold), and C to 3,065 on 02-Jul, which held the .50 retracement. Price then based and turned up into an early impulse (wave i) - the 21-22 Jul officials cleared the $3,160 pivot to 3,205 - but the 23-Jul official eased to cash $3,194 / 3M $3,182 (a minor wave (ii) pullback) and the traded 3M slipped to ~$3,165 on 24-Jul as the war premium narrowed. Because wave A was a five-wave move, alternation still argues a zigzag correction that has completed, keeping the base/impulse read alive. BASE CASE (52%): price holds above 3,085 and presses the 3,230 MA20 then the .382 at 3,260. RANGE ALTERNATE (35%): a stall between 3,085 and 3,260 while diplomacy and strikes trade off. BEAR ALTERNATE (13%): a revived ceasefire and a break below 3,085 opens a retest of 3,061.50. INVALIDATION: a daily close below 3,061.50 voids the base/impulse count; a decisive close above 3,260 confirms the next leg. Watch whether the cash-3M backwardation re-steepens from +$12 - curve confirmation is the tell. CONFIDENCE: moderate. Technical context only, not advice.

so_what.line: Aluminium's rebound paused on the latest official - the 23-Jul settlement printed cash $3,194 / 3M $3,182, trimming the cash-3M backwardation to +$12 - as the war-risk premium began to NARROW: Brent fell ~4% toward $96 on 24-Jul after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is trying to revive US-Iran talks, even as US strikes ran a 13th night. Stock still drew to a fresh 2022 low (275,175 t), keeping fundamentals tight beneath the softer tape.
points: What moved: the 23-Jul LME official eased (cash $3,194.00, -$11; 3M $3,182.00, -$3), narrowing the cash-3M backwardation from +$20 to +$12; the traded 3M slipped further to ~$3,165 on 24-Jul. A pause after two firm sessions, not a reversal - price is holding the rebound off the $3,085 four-month low.

Why: the geopolitical risk premium is narrowing. Brent fell ~3.9% to ~$96.7 on 24-Jul after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran talks - even as US Central Command ran a 13th straight night of strikes and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'. Escalation and de-escalation are running in parallel; the skew is two-sided again, not one-way.

Still tight: LME stock drew another 1,600 t to 275,175 t, a fresh low since 2022 (~-46% YTD), with SHFE also drawing and Macquarie flagging a ~930 kt 2026 deficit - no inventory buffer. The still-backwardated curve is the market pricing physical tightness even as the front eased.

Watch this week: whether US-Iran diplomacy firms (further war-premium unwind) or strikes re-escalate; the SHFE/LME arb, which has narrowed and threatens the record China export flow (June 711 kt); EGA's Al Taweelah alumina ramp and the deepening ex-China surplus (FOB Australia ~$322); and the $3,230/$3,260 resistance stack when the LME reopens Monday.

forward.basis: LME official prices via Westmetall. Baseline = LME 3-month official (a traded market price). Range = random-walk cone from realized volatility. Driver score = 3 transparent rules, hit rate measured on history.
forward.source: London Metal Exchange official settlements via Westmetall (https://www.westmetall.com/en/markdaten.php?action=table&field=LME_Al_cash)
forward.stance_label: Current physical-market condition (diagnostic, not a forecast)

drivers.name: Curve carry (cash − 3M)
drivers.rule: Backwardation (cash above 3M) = prompt physical tightness = bullish; contango = bearish.

drivers.name: Inventory trend (13-week)
drivers.rule: LME stock falling more than 2% over 13 weeks = tightening = bullish; rising >2% = bearish.

drivers.name: Momentum (3M vs 20-week average)
drivers.rule: Price above its 20-week average = uptrend = bullish; below = bearish.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 39.6% directional hit rate against a 73.3% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 2.32% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (96 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-04-24). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.
